Proof of Inference (PoI)

FLOP's work is inference, not hashing. A miner earns by executing an agent's inference session and leaving behind evidence that the work happened as specified.

What the proof is made of

Each session leaves activation commitments and a co-signed transcript. That evidence is the proof of inference: validators record it, and challengers can audit it later.

  • The model commits tiny fingerprints of its internal state during the session — TOPLOC commitments, 258 bytes per 32 tokens.
  • Every turn becomes a co-signed leaf under a Merkle root, and the chain stores that root at settlement.
  • A hardware quote is part of the proof only on the optional HARD tier.

Verification does not rest on trusted hardware

Every session must carry an activation commitment that a challenger can re-check, and disputes are settled by re-execution under bond. Confidential computing is an optional upgrade, not an entry requirement — see SOFT and HARD tiers.

Why this is cheap enough to work

The network never re-runs a whole session to trust it. A sampled check is one prefill — roughly 100x cheaper than generation — or a sub-cubic arithmetic check. Checking is dramatically cheaper than producing, which is what makes an audit lottery affordable.

What the proof does and does not establish

PoI establishes that the registered work was performed as specified. It does not establish that a model's answer is correct, safe, or high quality.

Status

Draft whitepaper. The SOFT tier is ratified and first-class, but its end-to-end settlement and dispute lane is still being specified, and the currently wired settlement path remains the attested one.
